items.markdown:
![How to Make a Delicious Vegan Thai Khao Soi - WoonHeng](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/07280323-1672-0139-0000-1dd59450ed35:6)
Khao soi uses `wheat-based egg noodles (often sold as wonton noodles)` , served both boiled in the soup and deep-fried until crispy. You can buy fresh or dried egg noodles at an Asian grocery store, or use Japanese ramen or rice noodles if needed.[](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gwV9SJtewCY&vl=en&t=484) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gwV9SJtewCY&vl=en&t=484)[[2]](https://hot-thai-kitchen.com/kao-soi/)[[3]](https://www.ediblememphis.com/the-best-khao-soi/)[[4]](https://www.feastingathome.com/thai-coconut-noodle-soup-khao-soi/)

The Two Noodle Styles You Need

- **Boiled Noodles:** Soft, flat or round Chinese egg noodles placed at the bottom of the bowl. Cook them in boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes.[](https://hot-thai-kitchen.com/kao-soi/) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3eOEqeff18U&t=29)
- **Crispy Fried Noodles:** A small portion of the same raw egg noodles, cut shorter and fried in hot oil for 30 to 60 seconds, then salted and put on top of the soup for crunch.[](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gwV9SJtewCY&vl=en&t=484) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OjZLlvM7CbM)[[2]](https://www.tiktok.com/@iankewks/video/7319538451332861189)[[3]](https://thewoksoflife.com/chicken-khao-soi/)

Tips for Cooking

- **Uncooked Noodles:** Buy raw flour-dusted egg noodles instead of pre-cooked ones so a portion can fry properly.
- **No Salt in Water:** Skip salt when boiling the noodles because the curry broth has plenty of flavor.
- **Substitutes:** Japanese ramen or standard wheat pasta like linguine work well if you cannot find Asian egg noodles.[](https://www.feastingathome.com/thai-coconut-noodle-soup-khao-soi/)
